name: store-heldout-v1
description: The 75 memories of store-v1 with 28 other questions, written before the first run of lexical_term_weights and so not used to choose its design: each has one memory that holds the answer, in the words of a question rather than of the memory. It checks a change to word search on questions that store-v1's 17 did not tune. It is a second set over the same memories, not a second corpus. Run it with --store-fixture and --baseline none.

memories.content: Alex Rivera is a senior backend engineer at Northwind Logistics, a freight-tracking startup with about 45 employees.
Alex joined Northwind in March 2024 as a backend engineer and was promoted to senior in January 2026.
Before Northwind, Alex worked at Meridian Freight in Brooklyn from 2019 to early 2024.
Alex lives in Denver, Colorado. Alex moved there from Brooklyn in March 2026 because Northwind is remote first.
Alex prefers concise explanations with the answer first and details only when asked.
Alex likes code examples in Go and TypeScript and dislikes Java examples.
Alex has a border collie named Juniper, adopted in 2024. Juniper needs a walk at 6:30 am and 6 pm.
Alex's partner is Jordan, a nurse practitioner. Jordan is allergic to shellfish.
Alex drinks black coffee and avoids caffeine after 2 pm.
Always give Alex time estimates in hours, not story points.
When Alex asks about databases, assume Postgres and skip the basics.
Assistant noted Alex's communication style: short messages, wants the conclusion in the first sentence, dislikes long preambles.
Alex uses Neovim as the main editor. Alex switched from VS Code in August 2026.
Alex went back to VS Code for the Go debugger but keeps Neovim for quick edits and writing.
Northwind runs on AWS: ECS Fargate for services, RDS Postgres for data, SQS for event delivery, and Datadog for observability.
The shipment_events table has 2.3 billion rows and grows by about 40 million rows per day.
The p99 latency of the shipment lookup endpoint is 480 ms. The target is under 150 ms.
Northwind decided to migrate shipment_events from one Postgres 14 instance to Postgres 16 with native range partitioning by week.

memories.speaker: Priya Shah
memories.content: I think we should look at TimescaleDB instead of native partitioning. Compression would save a lot of storage.
Assistant compared native partitioning with TimescaleDB. Native partitioning adds no new dependency. TimescaleDB gives compression but needs extra operations work.
Alex rejected TimescaleDB because RDS does not offer it and the team ruled out self-hosting Postgres.
Assistant suggested pg_partman to create and drop weekly partitions automatically.
Alex agreed to use pg_partman for partition management.
Add a covering index on (carrier_id, event_time) to bring shipment lookup latency down.
The staging dry run of the migration happened on 2026-09-12 and took 6 hours 40 minutes.
A runaway autovacuum on shipment_events caused a 22 minute degradation on 2026-10-02.
Production cutover is scheduled for Saturday 2026-10-24 at 02:00 UTC.

memories.speaker: Sam Lindqvist
memories.content: I found a replication lag risk on the read replicas. I want the cutover moved one week.
Correction: the production cutover moved from 2026-10-24 to Saturday 2026-10-31 at 02:00 UTC after Sam found the replica lag risk.
Rollback plan: keep the old table for 14 days behind a read-only view, and switch reads back if error rates rise above 1 percent.
Alex is on call the week of 2026-10-26, which overlaps the cutover.
Alex asked to swap the on-call week with Priya so the cutover is not during Alex's shift. Priya agreed.
Priya Shah is now on call the week of 2026-10-26. Alex covers the week of 2026-11-02.
Assistant drafted the cutover checklist: freeze writes, run final sync, verify row counts, flip the view, watch Datadog for 30 minutes.
Alex formats SQL with lowercase keywords and one clause per line.
The Datadog dashboard for this work is called Shipment Lookup SLO.
Alex's manager is Dana Okafor, VP of Engineering.
Priya Shah is a backend engineer on the platform team. Sam Lindqvist is the site reliability engineer.
Alex has a 1:1 with Dana every Tuesday at 10:00 Mountain time.

memories.speaker: Dana Okafor
memories.content: Please have Sam review the migration runbook before Friday.
Alex will present the migration plan at the engineering all-hands on 2026-10-21.
Alex prefers async written updates over meetings.
Alex likes pair programming and does it most Thursdays.
Correction: pair programming drains Alex. Alex prefers short 30 minute bursts and not full sessions.
Alex wants to reach a staff engineer role within 18 months.

memories.speaker: Dana Okafor
memories.content: I would like you to lead the observability rewrite next quarter. It would be good staff-level evidence.
Alex first declined to lead the observability rewrite, citing the migration workload.
Alex accepted leading the observability rewrite on 2026-10-14, on the condition that a second engineer joins the effort.
Assistant helped Alex outline a staff promotion packet: migration impact, observability leadership, and mentoring Priya.
Alex mentors Priya Shah in a weekly 30 minute session on Wednesdays.
Alex prefers Go for services and TypeScript for internal tooling.
Alex decided to use sqlc instead of an ORM for new services.
Alex dislikes ORMs after painful GORM migrations at Meridian Freight.
Alex writes table-driven tests in Go and wants subtests named after the scenario.
When reviewing Alex's code, point out race conditions and unchecked errors first.
Do not suggest adding dependencies unless the standard library cannot do the job.
Alex is learning Rust on weekends and is reading Rust for Rustaceans.
Assistant explained how Rust ownership maps onto Go's garbage collected model, using Alex's shipment parser as the example.
Alex chose OpenTelemetry for the observability rewrite, with Datadog as the backend.
Alex worries that high-cardinality metric tags will raise the Datadog bill. The current spend is about 6,200 USD per month.
Limit metric tags to carrier_id and region, and use traces for per-shipment detail.
Alex and Jordan plan a trip to Japan in April 2027 for the cherry blossom season.
Correction: the Japan trip moved earlier, to 2027-03-28 through 2027-04-11, because the blossoms peak in late March.
They chose Tokyo, Kyoto, Kanazawa, and Osaka. They dropped Hiroshima to save time.
Alex prefers trains to flights and wants a JR Pass for the Japan trip.
Alex likes ramen shops and izakaya and avoids touristy restaurants.
Because of Jordan's shellfish allergy, Alex needs a Japanese allergy card for restaurants.
The Japan trip budget is 8,500 USD, not including flights.
Alex booked United flights from Denver to Tokyo Haneda departing 2027-03-28.
Alex rides gravel bikes on weekends, about 60 miles a week.
Alex signed up for a 100 km gravel race in Fruita on 2026-11-07.
Alex strained a calf on 2026-10-09 and is skipping long rides for two weeks.
Assistant suggested a taper plan for the Fruita race: two easy rides the week before and a rest day on 2026-11-06.
Alex reads science fiction. The current book is Children of Time.
Alex wants to cut screen time after 9 pm.
